shortDescription: The German spot power contract fell in early trading on Wednesday on expectations of increased renewable energy supply across the region.($1 = 0.8659 euros)

children: The German spot power contract fell in early trading on Wednesday on expectations of increased renewable energy supply across the region.
The German day-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBD1) fell 23.7% to €142 ($164) per megawatt-hour at 0745 GMT, LSEG data showed.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) dropped 23.4% to €137/MWh, the data showed.
Renewable supply is expected to climb in Germany with wind power output seen jumping 9.9 gigawatts to 23.2 GW while solar supply is expcted to rise 200 megawatts, LSEG data showed.
French wind supply is seen up more marginally, adding 1 GW to 5.9 GW, the data showed.
German wind supply should reduce thermal generation, with residual load in the country expected to decrease to an average of around 15 GW over the next five days, EnergyScan analysts said.
French nuclear availability was flat at 80% of total capacity.
Workers at the Flamanville 2 reactor remained on strike on Wednesday, with power at the reactor cut by 1 GW until midday, according to EDF data.
On the forward side, the German year-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) fell 0.6% to €129/MWh, the data showed.

German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche plans to use market incentives to encourage traders to keep more gas available this winter, while avoiding direct state gas purchases, amid concerns over supply, a government source told Reuters.

Germany's SEFE, a gas importer under government control, said on Wednesday it had independently decided to increase natural gas storage and had not been ordered by the German economy ministry to do so.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) was untraded after closing at €87/MWh, LSEG data showed.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
was down 0.7% to €84.96 a metric ton.
